title: Unbounded section derived unit from affine-basis acyclicity
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], V an affine open, and F an integer-indexed complex of O_X-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For each affine W contained in V, suppose all positive sheaf cohomology groups of F^n restricted to W, of Coker(d^{n-1}) restricted to W, and of H^n(F) restricted to W vanish, for every n. Cohomology is that of the underlying abelian sheaf, as in the source library Scheme.Modules.H [def-sc-sheaf-cohomology-functor]. Let S be evaluation at V, valued in O_X(V)-modules. In chosen derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the canonical derived unit Q_h(S(F)) -> R(S)(Q_h(F)) is invertible. No quasi-coherence or boundedness is assumed; the empty affine open is included.

source.place: Tag 08C2, lemma-alternating-cech-complex-complex-ss, singleton cover of V; proof read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08C2. Compatible tower: Tag 071B; restriction: Tag 08BS.

proof.text: Restrict F to V. The affine opens W contained in V form a basis, including V itself. Their sheaf cohomology is exactly that appearing in the three hypotheses. Apply the singleton covering of V in Tag 08C2. Open restriction preserves K-injectivity, so resolving on X and restricting computes the same derived sections as resolving on V.

For bounded-below F the termwise basis acyclicity makes the acyclic Cech comparison invertible (the bounded-below case in 08C2). The singleton alternating Cech total is just the ordinary section complex. For general F, its good truncation in degrees at least -m has a differential cokernel as its lowest term. Thus both term and differential-cokernel hypotheses verify the bounded-below criterion for every truncation. Restriction is exact, so the cokernels and cohomology used after restriction are the restrictions of the specified objects.

Use the cohomology-sheaf hypothesis with d=0 in the compatible resolution tower construction of Tag 071B. Its inverse limit is a K-injective resolution of the restricted F, and sections commute with this inverse limit. In each degree, the singleton section complexes of the good truncations are eventually identical, and their section cohomology is eventually constant. Consequently the first derived limit of the cohomology tower vanishes and the Milnor sequence identifies cohomology of the limit with that constant value. This proves invertibility of the canonical ordinary-to-derived comparison, rather than merely existence of some isomorphism.

The module-valued comparison is the derived unit of evaluation S, transported from the homotopy quotient. It is identified with the abelian-sheaf comparison in 08C2 because injective module sheaves are flasque and hence section-acyclic as abelian sheaves. The exact conservative forgetful functor from modules to abelian groups detects its invertibility. If V is empty, evaluation is the zero functor and the same conclusion follows.

lean.statement:
theorem affineBasisSections_isIso_derivedUnit
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (V : X.Opens) (hV : IsAffineOpen V)
    (F : CochainComplex X.Modules ℤ)
    [HasDerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [HasDerivedCategory
      (ModuleCat.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).obj.obj (op V)))]
    (hterms : ∀ (W : X.Opens), IsAffineOpen W → W ≤ V → ∀ (n : ℤ) (q : ℕ),
      Subsingleton (((F.X n).restrict W.ι).H (q + 1)))
    (hcokernels : ∀ (W : X.Opens), IsAffineOpen W → W ≤ V → ∀ (n : ℤ) (q : ℕ),
      Subsingleton (((cokernel (F.d (n - 1) n)).restrict W.ι).H (q + 1)))
    (hhomology : ∀ (W : X.Opens), IsAffineOpen W → W ≤ V → ∀ (n : ℤ) (q : ℕ),
      Subsingleton (((F.homology n).restrict W.ι).H (q + 1))) :
    let S := SheafOfModules.evaluation.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) (op V)
    letI : S.Additive := inferInstanceAs
      ((SheafOfModules.forget.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) ⋙
        PresheafOfModules.evaluation.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).obj (op V)).Additive)
    IsIso (S.rightDerivedFunctorUnit.app ((HomotopyCategory.quotient _ _).obj F))
